title: Your first report
text: Create a first draft from one source. Install the desktop app and open a separate workspace for sources, drafts, conversations and task records. In settings, select an installed, authenticated runtime and model. Confirm that your source may be sent to that service. Create a report. Specify the audience, date range, questions and target length, then add one public source. After starting, follow progress on the waiting page or switch to a saved draft. My reports shows stages, queue time and execution time; open the body to check citations and edit. Generate Word from the export menu. Download the completed file and open it in Word or WPS. Success means a saved draft version and a Word file you can open. A queued task or download button alone is not proof of completion. Without a model account, read these guides first. If your installed version offers a synthetic sample, it can demonstrate editing and export without a model; it is not an independently reviewed, model-generated report.

title: Install and update
text: Choose the right installer and preserve your workspace. Choose the Apple silicon DMG or Windows x64 EXE on the download page. Check About This Mac for the chip; browser Intel labels are unreliable. Prepare Python 3.11 or later. A compatible existing 3.12 installation is supported; the app neither requires a new 3.11 download nor installs system Python automatically. On Mac, copy the app to Applications. On Windows, run the installer. Follow the first-launch steps to prepare app-specific dependencies. Install and authenticate a model CLI separately. Desktop bridges use Electron’s built-in Node; WebUI bridge runtimes need Node.js 20+. Save drafts and back up the entire workspace while tasks are idle. Check updates in settings. On Mac, replace the app in Finder; Windows uses its installer. Version 0.22.1 fixes an OpenCode service startup timeout encountered in the Windows desktop app. Update the desktop app before retrying if you encounter this issue. After restarting, check the app version and open the original workspace to confirm drafts and sources. The PyPI package provides the service and WebUI, not the desktop app. Initial Mac and Windows packages are unsigned; Mac packages are also not notarized. Verify the official source and SHA256, then use the OS permission for that app rather than disabling system protection. If updates fail, use official Releases; do not delete the workspace to fix a download.

title: Models and costs
text: Understand execution, data recipients and billing. Choose BriefLoop Agent or Agent CLI in settings. Configure a model service directly for the built-in agent; for a CLI, sign in or configure its API in that tool first. Usage is charged to the selected service account. Use a model and reasoning option that the current runtime supports. Version 0.25.0 supports OpenCode 1.x and 2.x; configure v2 providers in OpenCode. Saving settings is not a successful connection test: verify with a short public-text conversation. The main agent, Evaluator, Wiki Maintainer and Skill Proposer can use separate models. Evaluation and learning may also consume model usage. Set research limits, length and execution time. These are not a complete monetary cap; metering of runtime-native search varies. Check actual quotas and bills with the model and search providers. BriefLoop does not supply their subscriptions or model credits. The first conversation should return an actual response. New tasks use saved settings; queued and running tasks retain their original configuration. For quota errors, 429, 503 or an unknown model, inspect the task error and runtime authentication. Matching model names do not imply shared subscriptions. Read-only and network controls vary by runtime.

title: Search and task progress
text: Choose search channels, fix the reporting period and follow actual progress. In Settings → Run and search, choose a preferred channel and allowed supplements. New workspaces prefer Tavily and allow runtime-native search to supplement it. Enable Bocha or Zhipu explicitly and configure their keys. Choose cross-market coverage checks, gap-only supplementation or preferred-channel only. Tavily, Bocha and Zhipu use separate accounts. Without a search key, choose DuckDuckGo or capabilities already available in your runtime. Check the cutoff, date range and time zone before starting. The run retains its search policy and time window; later settings apply to new tasks. Scheduled reports recalculate relative dates for each run. In My reports, follow the current stage, elapsed time, successful and failed searches, saved sources, research rounds, review and revisions. Open saved drafts early; stop or resume the original task when needed. Open Research budget → Search records for channels, purpose, duration and errors. Filter sources by their discovery channel. Choose research depth, fact-checking and automatic learning when creating a report. Target duration guides the task; it does not stop the run at that time. The separate advanced maximum-runtime safeguard is off by default. Deep research defaults to a 10,000-character target and 12,000-character cap; explicit length settings take precedence. Set simultaneous reports in settings: the default is 4, with a range of 1–16. Scout concurrency is separate. A dedicated waiting page shows pending generation, while the version selector lets you open saved drafts. Queue time and execution time are shown separately. Stages and counts come from recorded execution and artifacts, without an estimated completion percentage. Failed searches remain visible and consume search-attempt quota. Unmetered runtime-native search is shown as unknown rather than included in controlled API counts. Search snippets, saved sources and successful queries do not establish factual accuracy. There are no dedicated WeChat or Xiaohongshu connectors.

title: Write and edit reports
text: Move from sources and requirements to an editable draft. Create a report with its audience, purpose, required questions and language. Version 0.25.0 supports English reports. Check and freeze the cutoff, date range and time zone before starting; keep historical sources tied to their own periods. Add original sources; use search snippets only as discovery leads. Check dates, entities and definitions. Read conclusions and tables, then inspect key citations. Working drafts remain visible and downloadable even with low scores or unresolved review issues. Edit and save the body, or give BriefLoop specific revision instructions. Preserve the original and confirm that changes create a new version. After saving, download Word or select HTML or PDF from the export menu. Version 0.25.0 adds Excel, with one worksheet per table or the full report on one sheet; basic export needs no OfficeCLI. Export uses the saved version fixed when requested; later edits require another export. The body, version history and exported content should correspond. Edit in the browser and check final pagination in Word or WPS. If generation fails, inspect task logs and saved artifacts before recovering. Do not submit duplicate reports as a substitute for recovery. Unsaved edits do not appear in an earlier export.

title: Sources and review
text: Distinguish saved, linked, scored and reviewed content. Open citations to inspect the source title, date and excerpt, and consult originals where needed. For important figures, check entity, period, units, denominators and calculations. Preserve source conflicts rather than resolving them with a secondary summary. Read scores and specific findings for the current version; an old score does not automatically apply to a rewritten draft. Version 0.25.0 offers standard or strict review in settings. Standard review checks the draft, sources and task history in an independent read-only session using Codex, OpenCode or BriefLoop Agent. Strict review currently uses BriefLoop Agent to enforce packet and tool limits; unsupported runtimes cannot silently downgrade it. Inspect the actual mode and unchecked items. Historical reviews with no recorded mode are not labeled strict. Both modes use the same factual and evidence standards. Ask BriefLoop to revise findings, or edit and save yourself, then check the new version. Downloading a working draft is separate from eligibility for formal delivery. Each resolved issue should correspond to a change in the new version, with review scope and unresolved issues visible. A source link or binding alone is not factual proof. Scanned PDFs, images and Excel formulas without cached values may need additional checks. Do not call a draft formally deliverable while it contains material errors, core evidence gaps or unresolved material conflicts.

title: Templates and charts
text: Manage writing methods, layout and chart data separately. Specify the report purpose, language and content before choosing a Word layout. Version 0.25.0 adds 10 English layouts. A template name does not establish a specialized research workflow. Upload a DOCX for a company template and inspect recognized sections and manual fields. Supported layouts depend on the installed version. After table edits, check units, rows, columns and totals. Charts should retain sources and data periods. When asking BriefLoop to change complex charts, request checks against linked data; appearance alone does not verify values. Save, export and inspect fonts, pagination, table widths and captions in Word or WPS. The downloaded document should retain required sections and readable tables and figures. Layout changes and content edits are separate; verify the exported file. Complex Office objects, nested tables and multi-section templates may not be fully supported. Keep originals and inspect specific errors rather than assuming unsupported content was imported. The web editor is not a Word pagination preview.

title: Feedback and reuse
text: Turn specific revisions into inspectable, reversible experience. Explain the desired writing behavior or reason for a correction, including when it applies, rather than leaving only a score. Choose whether to enable automatic learning in settings and set the maximum rounds K. Additional rounds can increase model usage and time. Inspect Wiki experience and proposed skills. The Wiki holds method knowledge, not current-period evidence. Inspect validation results and adoption status. A candidate file does not mean it is active, and a running task does not demonstrate a benefit. If adoption is unsuitable, use the rollback control available in your version and confirm the active skill state. Preserve original feedback and comparison records. You should be able to distinguish feedback, candidates, validation and active content. Feedback can become experience evaluated for adoption; scores are not guaranteed to improve every round. When paused or out of quota, keep records and follow recovery instructions. Policies for explicit human requirements versus automated scoring suggestions vary by version; do not assume a development policy exists in an older installer.

title: FAQ and data
text: Preserve drafts, stop tasks and understand data transfers. Workspaces and records are stored locally. Cloud-model use sends relevant task, source, draft or feedback content to the selected service. Search queries go to the search provider and web requests to target sites. MCP parameters and necessary credentials go to the configured connector; local stdio programs may also access the network. Disabling public search does not stop model data transfers or guarantee network isolation for every runtime. Custom gateways and proxies may receive requests too. Use the app’s stop control and wait for a terminal state. Closing a browser does not stop an independent service; follow desktop save and task prompts when exiting. Back up the entire workspace while tasks are idle. Check materials and personal information before sharing logs, audit packages or folders, and exclude credentials. Saved drafts and sources should remain accessible after failure. Deleting local copies does not delete data already received by third parties; their retention rules depend on the service and account configuration. Diagnose HTTP 403, download and dependency errors by stage rather than repeatedly uninstalling and deleting workspaces. Record the version and error, use official releases and runtime diagnostics, and remove credentials and sensitive content before public support requests.

title: External agents and CLI
text: Let your agent submit reports, save revisions and download version-bound Word files. Install the briefloop CLI and open the intended workspace on the same machine. Configure its model, sources and company-context choice. Run discover and proceed only when ready=true. Run skill to obtain the protocol shipped with your installed version. Inspect source IDs, submit with a stable request_id, and query the returned job_id. Preserve failures and any saved drafts. Read a specific version. Revise with the complete editor_document and base_version. Export, query artifact_available, then download. Real job and version IDs are returned; the CLI verifies the downloaded Word hash. Drafts, revisions and task state stay linked. This connects to an existing local service, not a remote MCP server. Submit uses the workspace model and its billing; revise saves edits made by the external agent. Formal delivery still uses existing checks. Do not edit SQLite directly or retry an unknown result with a new request_id.
